original_question: Classify all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane that have exactly three unbalanced vertices.
target_in_paper: Section 3.1, Problem 3.1.5: Classify all geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane with 3 unbalanced vertices.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct object (geodesic multinets), the correct ambient space (the Euclidean plane), and the correct three-unbalanced-vertex regime. It matches the paper's stated open problem essentially verbatim, except that the paper says "with 3 unbalanced vertices" rather than "that have exactly three unbalanced vertices."
missing_details: The paper's target is an open problem, specifically Section 3.1, Problem 3.1.5; it is not the neighboring rigidity theorem for geodesic nets (Theorem 3.1.2), which concerns nets rather than multinets.

To be stand-alone, the question must define a geodesic multinet: a finite connected multigraph in the Euclidean plane whose edges are straight line segments between vertices, each endowed with a positive integer multiplicity.
It must state the balancing condition at every balanced vertex: the multiplicity-weighted sum of the unit tangent vectors along all incident edges, directed away from the vertex, is zero.
It should make explicit that the three distinguished vertices are the unbalanced (boundary) vertices, i.e. balancing is not required there.
The paper works under standing conventions that all considered geodesic (multi)nets are connected.

The paper suppresses balanced vertices of degree 2, since such vertices can be inserted or removed without changing the essential net; accordingly, all balanced vertices under the paper's conventions have degree at least 3 and are non-isolated.

The paper also excludes edges whose two endpoints are both unbalanced, because such edges can be added or removed without affecting balancing at balanced vertices; your draft leaves this convention implicit.

The official problem does not fix the locations of the three unbalanced vertices in advance, so the classification is over all geodesic multinets in \mathbb{R}^2 having exactly three unbalanced vertices, not only for one prescribed triple.
refined_question: Classify, under the standing conventions of the paper, all connected geodesic multinets in the Euclidean plane \mathbb{R}^2 with exactly three unbalanced (boundary) vertices; that is, classify all finite connected multigraphs in \mathbb{R}^2 whose edges are straight line segments endowed with positive integer multiplicities, for which at every balanced vertex the multiplicity-weighted sum of the unit tangent vectors along the incident edges is zero, where degree-2 balanced vertices are suppressed, balanced vertices are non-isolated, and no edge has both endpoints unbalanced.
justification: The draft is targeting the exact open problem stated in Section 3.1, Problem 3.1.5. The nearby context confirms this: Example 3.1.1 exhibits multinets with three unbalanced vertices and many balanced vertices, Theorem 3.1.2 gives the contrasting rigidity result for geodesic nets with three unbalanced vertices, and Problems 3.1.3 and 3.1.4 are narrower neighboring questions about the same three-vertex multinet regime. To make the problem self-contained and faithful to the paper, one must import the definition of geodesic multinets and the Euclidean balancing condition from Section 1, together with the paper's standing conventions on connectedness, suppression of degree-2 balanced vertices, and exclusion of edges between unbalanced vertices.
